abstract.t: This document describes a technology-neutral architecture for age assurance on the Internet, drawing on the framework established by ISO/IEC 27566-1 and the levels of assurance defined in IEEE 2089.1. It sets out the methods of age assurance (verification, estimation and inference), how their performance is measured and assured, the roles and trust relationships involved, and how results can be reused across services without creating persistent identifiers. Its main contribution is a model for communicating trustworthy, privacy- preserving age assertions between independently governed systems. It treats assurance, privacy, interoperability, resistance to circumvention and inclusion as measurable properties of complete age assurance systems, and distinguishes the capabilities of existing technical components from the additional safeguards necessary for secure and privacy-preserving deployment. It is neutral on whether age restrictions should exist, at what ages and for which services, which are policy questions outside its scope; it is not neutral about how safely and privately such restrictions are implemented where they do exist.
